subject: Kickoff: BlueWave inference economics & tuning plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: BlueWave inference economics & tuning plan

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As promised, here's a practical kickoff note focused on the cost/performance work we'll run during onboarding. Goal: get you to steady-state SLA (95th p99 latency targets) while reducing token cost per request by 20–40% where feasible.

High-level plan (3 phases):
1) Discovery (this week): collect request traces, sequence length distribution, prompt prefixes, and a sample of requests that exercise edge flows. We need a ~48–72h trace to build a representative batch/caching profile.
2) Baseline & experiments (1–2 weeks): run controlled bench tests for batching profiles, prefix/KV caching rules, and 2 quantization profile candidates. We'll measure latency distributions and objective cost per 10k tokens.
3) Rollout & monitoring (ongoing): staged rollout with canary traffic split + automatic fallback policy. We'll monitor quality regressions against the prompt set and have rollback windows.

Key asks from BlueWave:
- Provide a 48h request trace (anonymized) or enable the temporary trace collector we sent last week.
- Confirm latency SLOs (p95, p99) and the percentage of requests that are interactive vs. batch.

Attachments: bluewave-inference-discovery.pdf (brief checklist & sample tracing snippet).

Proposed next steps: can we schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to confirm the trace path and agree on the mutual action plan? I can include Monica (CS lead) and Grace (performance engineer) to scope the bench runs.

Thanks —
Jonas
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Anna Lee <anna@bluewave.ai>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: BlueWave inference economics & tuning plan

Thanks Jonas — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifying questions before the sync:
- For quantization: do you plan to run int8-style conversion in our environment, or will you keep a float fallback? Our security team asks about validation steps.
- For batching: what's the expected latency uplift for a 4–8 request batch for our median sequence length (~120 tokens)?

We can provide the trace; I'll ask infra to drop a bucket link. Tomorrow 10:30am PT works for a quick call.

— Anna
VP Product, BlueWave.ai
anna@bluewave.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@bluewave.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BlueWave inference economics & tuning plan

Anna — great questions. Short answers before our call:
- Quantization approach: we'll test two candidate profiles (dynamic int8 with calibration and a mixed 4-bit profile) during the baseline experiments. There will be a float32 fallback in the canary so requests that show quality drift use the fallback automatically. We'll also provide validation scripts and a short QA checklist so your security/compliance team can reproduce the tests.
- Batching: for median length ~120 tokens, our bench suggests 4-request batching increases median latency by ~12–18ms on A100-series hardware but reduces cost per token by ~22% in typical seq distribution; we will provide exact numbers after the initial trace.

I've attached the mutual action plan draft (bluewave-map-v1.xlsx) to capture owners and timelines. On the call we'll lock owners and the measurement rubric (latency percentiles + hallucination rate on the prompt set).

Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Anna Lee <anna@bluewave.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BlueWave inference economics & tuning plan — perf notes

Anna / team — tagging a few technical notes I'll run in the baseline bench and what I'd like from your infra:

Bench plan (short):
- Run baseline at target concurrency and two traffic shapes: interactive (p95 latency target 450ms) and bursty (API spikes).
- Batching sweep: batch sizes = [1,2,4,8], with a latency SL margin check and cost/token calc.
- Caching: evaluate prefix/KV cache with 10m/1h TTLs for common prompt prefixes; measure cache hit rate and effect on upstream token count.
- Quant profiles: q4_0 (4-bit mixed), int8_dynamic (calibrated), float32 baseline. We'll compute quality deltas on the prompt evaluation set and surface token-cost wins.
- Routing policy suggestion: Primary route to rwd-lowlat-3 (low-latency variant) for 90% of interactive traffic; fallback to rwd-eco-2 for cost-sensitive async workloads. Canary split 5% initially.

Expected artifacts after baseline: CSV of latency buckets, token-cost per profile, quality diffs (BLEU/ROUGE or custom prompts), and a recommended rollout plan. I'll attach the initial benchmark run (benchmarks-5k-steps.csv) after the first run.

Grace O'Connor
Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
